title.narrative: Share-Net International

description.narrative:
Share-Net International (SNI), the knowledge platform on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), combines the expertise and strengths of development organisations, Southern partners and key international actors in the field of SRHR to achieve the SRHR and HIV related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Membership includes universities, knowledge institutes, development organisations, civil society organisations, media outlets, students and individual experts in the field of SRHR. The Platform encompasses national knowledge networks in four countries: Bangladesh, Burundi, Jordan and the Netherlands. These networks serve as conduits for situation assessments, defining research priorities, facilitating research participation by country institutions and hosting the local knowledge base/platform. They stimulate the participation of key international partners and regional and national SRHR actors. SNI aims to strengthen linkages between research, policy and practice through sharing, generating, translating and promoting the use of knowledge for the development of better policies and practices in SRHR.
The main services of SNI and its country hubs include •Meetings, discussions, (de-)briefings: SNI organises a diverse range of meetings focused around relevant topics or give (de-)briefings of global happenings. Furthermore, SNI coordinates activities planned or initiated by members. •Communities of Practice are at the heart of SNI and operate in each country hub, are context specific and create common ground for members while engaging in dialogues and activities. Under this networking outcome, SNI acts as a matchmaker; promoting interactions between the members of the CoPs and encouraging them to share knowledge which facilitates learning and ultimately, using this knowledge to improve policy and practice. •Share-Net International Rapid Improvement Model promotes knowledge exchange between the country hubs, aiming to oImprove understanding of which knowledge translation strategies contribute to change in SRHR policy or practice in the specific context of each country hub. oDevelop the capacity of the participating staff in the hubs for knowledge management and brokering oFacilitate learning, collaboration and exchange between country hubs. •SNI Co-Creation Conference aims at translating knowledge into products that allow SNI members and other participants to improve policy and practice on selected SRHR themes. Next to the development of these knowledge products, the Co-Creation Conference promotes uptake of knowledge in SRHR programmes, policies and practice through the development and presentation of narrative reviews and evidence briefs on the selected topics. •Online activities (website, newsletters) share relevant knowledge and resources on SRHR with the wider public making SRHR information accessible to all.

Description of how CoPs on SRHR are functioning

comment.narrative: Not measured at baseline

At Share-Net International, we have ongoing activities and strategies that maintain enthusiasm and keep members engaged in the iCoP. Members of an iCoP meet regularly based on an agreed-upon schedule, which can be monthly or every six weeks. The chair team for each meeting is composed of CoP members, supported by the SNI secretariat's CoP facilitator. A chair rotation is pre-determined and planned for the entire year, encouraging active member participation before and during meetings, while also helping them develop facilitation skills. Additionally, CoP members collaborate on knowledge products related to their interests, further stimulating engagement within the CoP. However, greater member ownership of the iCoP could enhance SNI's facilitation. Therefore, iCoPs should be initiated by groups of members rather than by SNI. The digital platform should offer the option to request the creation of an iCoP on a specific topic, thus shifting responsibility to the members and giving them a sense of greater accountability. Once a request to create a CoP is approved, SNI would only need to oversee the work and provide support as needed. Finally, implementing a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation plan with clear evaluation points can improve the CoP's functionality by allowing reflection on what didn�t work and finding solutions to identified issues. �Quote: �One of the key successes of this iCoP is that it has a specific target goal: to produce a knowledge product that gives each member a sense of ownership.� Quote: �The iCoP is a place where SRHR topics are discussed, which makes me realize and learn that the global environment on the topic differs among places and different challenges arise.�

However, with the increase of Share-Net International members around the world, we decided to set up 3 international communities of practice at an international level. Success Story #1: Activation grant as a sustainable and inclusive opportunity for Share-Net members Through its activation grants, Share-Net International (SNI) wants to give more consideration to vulnerable groups such as young people and people living with disabilities and advocates for inclusiveness as one of the core values of the projects it funds. In this success story, the Center for Research and Intervention for Individual, Community, and Social Development (CRIDIS) at the University of Burundi, one of our recipients of this year's Activation Grants, shares the success of their experience. CRIDIS worked on a project to improve the knowledge of young people and adolescents with disabilities regarding SRHR. Beforehand, a baseline study funded by SNI small grants was conducted in 2021 to identify the level of knowledge, attitudes, and practices of young people and adolescents living with disabilities regarding SRHR. This baseline study showed that adolescents and young people living with disabilities had a limited level of knowledge in terms of SRHR. It had also shown that access to information for this category is limited and that their sources of information on SRHR were unreliable, which had as a corollary the adoption of risky attitudes and practices. Thus, CRIDIS started this second project to improve the knowledge of young people and adolescents living with disabilities thanks to the SNI activation grant in 2022. Different knowledge products have been created, such as a training of trainers guide based on eight themes in SDSR. From this guide, a manual for the training of adolescents and young people has been extracted to provide these young people and adolescents living with disabilities with the knowledge required in SDSR. In addition, a Braille transcription of this manual has been made to enable young people and adolescents living with visual impairments to access the knowledge product. As mentioned by R�v�rien NSHIMIRIMANA, this project was an opportunity for CRIDIS to identify the needs of young people and adolescents living with disabilities in terms of SRHR, but also to realize their capacities despite their disability. In the various achievements of the project, teenage girls and young girls from two centers were trained to manufacture washable and reusable pads as part of their empowerment to obtain sanitary pads during menstruation. In addition, this project has enabled the various members of CRIDIS to collaborate with other actors, such as the Union of Disabled People of Burundi (UPHB), the National Program for Health and Reproduction (PNSR) under the Ministry of public health and AIDS control of Burundi as well as other stakeholders in the field of SDSR. The knowledge products resulting from this project have enabled CRIDIS, in its various activities, to strengthen the capacities of the managers and supervisors of the centers which shelter these young adolescents living with disabilities to equip them with the knowledge necessary to inform young people correctly. But also to train peer educators using the manual to educate their peers in the centers and beyond. Success Story #2: International Community of Practice (iCoP), a new element of collaboration and exchange between Share-Net member countries. Communities of practice (CoP) are essential in knowledge management at Share-Net International (SNI). Until 2021, the CoPs were held at the national level per hub. Various interesting knowledge products have been produced over the years within its CoPs. However, the knowledge generated was not sufficiently shared between the different hubs and other countries hosting SNI members. This is why SNI began establishing iCoPs in 2022. In this success story, Lizzie Jackson from CHOICE shares her experience setting up the iCoP on Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR) in adolescents and young people. The iCoP on SRHR among young people and adolescents was launched in December 2022 after a 9-month preparatory period during which the CoP facilitators from the hubs of Burundi, Burkina Faso, and Jordan by collaborating with the knowledge management experts of SNI have met several times to brainstorm and establish the purpose and objectives of this iCoP. It was also a platform for exchanges between the different hubs on the work carried out at the national level. Then other members of the iCoP were invited to join at the launch. Lizzie Jackson has had a positive experience setting up this iCoP. Compared to her previous experiences in other working groups, she finds that the composition of iCoP members is very diverse, with participants from different countries. It is also a great experience to work with the members during the preparation of the next iCoP session. Therefore, this iCoP meets its expectations regarding learning about the functioning of CoPs and the facilitation of sessions. Also, the atmosphere is very respectful. Another positive point is that translation using Wordly is available during the sessions and allows non-English speaking participants to follow and participate in their preferred languages. The way the facilitation of the sessions is organized in the rotation is really good. This makes it possible to engage all members to participate in the CoP actively but also to know their tasks and responsibilities. To improve the facilitation of iCoPs, it is important to hold informative and interactive sessions. This will facilitate knowledge sharing and member contribution, and engagement. Another important element that keeps members engaged is the nature of the topic on which the iCoP will focus. In addition, the regularity of meetings every two months makes it possible to keep the iCoP active without overloading the group members. Regarding communication, Lizzie appreciates that all iCoP-related information is usually sent in one email. So members are not overloaded with lots of emails. Success story #3: Co-Creation Conference. �For global problems we need to find global solutions. But not solutions that are developed in privileged spaces, like international organisations such as the united nations. But in global spaces with people who work in the different communities in the world to guarantee human rights. And that is what this conference allowed�. (Adriana Marcela Perez Rodriguez, Observatorio de Genero de Santander). As stated in the quote above, the Share-Net International Co-Creation Conference aims to bring together people from different background and expertise to work together in the development of a knowledge product that will aim to influence policy and practice at the global level. Co-creating with a diverse group of people allows for inspiration, creativity, out-of-the box solutions and cross-country learning which translate into products that are versatile enough to be used in different context where challenges on sexual and reproductive rights are faced. During the in-person co-creation conference in 2022, 8 participants were interviewed and all of them really appreciated the exchange and learning between people with different backgrounds. They could exchange best practices and lessons learned on �Access to quality sexual and reproductive health and right information�. This gave some tools and ideas to advance SRHR in different contexts. � It is the first time that I see people from different countries, from different cultures, different continents and different areas but that are working for the same causes. And this is something very important that I learnt. And I learnt also how things are working in those countries, and that I can use to change or improve our practices in Burkina Faso�. (Zalissa Bande, Share-Net Burkina Faso). Finally, the co-creation conference is an event that brings together people working on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights all over the world, it creates a safe space where people can feel that they belong and they are not along working to ensure sexual and reproductive health and rights for all. �When you talk about sexuality in my country, it is like you are a crazy person, you are not understood. Here, I saw many people who works on the same topic as me and it was great. It was like: wow I am not the only crazy person in this world�. (Gentille Nahimana, ZenPlanet Magazine)

Success Story 1: Activation grant as a means to support breaking the silence around sensitive topics. Dr Zaid Al-Hamdan from the Jordan University of Sciences and Technology (JUST) has had the opportunity to tackle the sensitive topic of sexual harassment in the universities in Jordan through a grant awarded last year by Share-Net International. He worked on a project entitled Breaking the Silence: Sexual Harassment at Jordan Universities.Quote: �I feel happy because I have broken the silence and raised awareness around this topic.�Dr Zaid mentioned that the main learning point is that tackling a sensitive issue is difficult in the context of Jordan because of cultural sensitivity. The population doesn�t want to discuss the topic, and everyone will start blaming you and asking why you chose this topic or what/ who is behind your project. Moreover, it�s challenging to obtain ethical approval for the project. Besides many questions to answer and to meet with several authorities, it was necessary at some point to even revise the study title to give it a chance to be approved. Although the study questions remained the same, the titles presented to the students differed. Instead of sexual harassment in the universities, it was in the communities.Succes Story 2: �Kenyan LGBTQI+ voices to be heard�. Joe received the Activation Grant in 2022. The goal of the grant was to conduct research on LGBTQI+ rights in Kenya with his organization Unplugged, now known as Rights & Freedoms Network. The last national study on this topic was conducted in 2011 and was outdated. Quote: �The research provided the opportunity to give workshops to health care workers. We have actually seen some change, especially from the hospitals that participated in the research. They have seen that there's more acceptance [towards the LGBTQI+ community].�Unplugged assembled a team comprising other organizations working with the LGBTQI+ community. Joe explained that many of these organizations operate underground due to fear of government repercussions, despite their presence in Kenya. The teams were organized and began collecting primary data, as there was insufficient secondary data available in their area at the time. The teams conducted interviews with various stakeholders to assess the status of the LGBTQI+ community in specific Kenyan districts, resulting in the generation of "fresh, new data" and a comprehensive report.
